name: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.20 ppm

significance.note: This is a precision remeasurement, not framed by the collaboration around a single sigma-significance figure in the material read (2026-09-17); no value is given rather than a guess.

summary.plain: A second Fermilab measurement of the same muon property, using data from 2019 and 2020 with more than four times as many positrons as the first result. The systematic error is reduced by more than a factor of 2, and the new experimental world average is a factor of 2 more precise.
summary.technical: Run-2 and Run-3 data (collected in 2019 and 2020) with more than 4 times the number of positrons from muon decay than the previous result from 2018 data; the systematic error is reduced by more than a factor of 2. these data alone give aμ = 116,592,057(25)×10⁻¹¹ (0.21 ppm), and combined with the 2018 result aμ(FNAL) = 116,592,055(24)×10⁻¹¹ (0.20 ppm); the new experimental world average aμ(exp) = 116,592,059(22)×10⁻¹¹ (0.19 ppm) represents a factor of 2 improvement in precision.

title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 0.20 ppm
why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says a precise measurement of the muon magnetic anomaly provides a stringent test of the Standard Model, whose prediction is made with high precision, and that any deviation between experiment and theory may be a sign of physics beyond the Standard Model.
